summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored documents from small jurisdictions (Uruguay, Luxembourg, Moldova, Papua New Guinea, Barbados, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Estonia, France, Ghana, Croatia, Lithuania, Monaco, Mexico, Samoa). Almost all are laws, regulations, bills and official pages: the pass adds programme rules (program_terms) and dated events, no new statistics (the Luxembourg counts were already recorded and add up to the printed 9). Points for review: (1) Luxembourg launch date: Bill 8586 says the investor title came from the law of 20 March 2017, the Finance Ministry FAQ and programs.csv say 8 March 2017; the new launch event uses the bill's date and says so. (2) Uruguay: the consolidated decree now has investment-linked tax-benefit thresholds (arts. 5-QUINQUIES to 5-SEPTIES, Decreto 188/026 of 10 Aug 2026); recorded as terms with routes starting tax_, they are not residence thresholds and should not enter the headline price. (3) Costa Rica forestry route (US$100,000, art. 92) and Mexico real-estate case (40,000 days of minimum wage) are lower or alternative routes; recorded as terms, check headline prices. (4) Ghana and Botswana have no programme rows; Ghana's bill clause 39 (CBI law to be enacted) is the only programme item.

events.title: First parliamentary vote on the dual citizenship constitutional amendment
events.description: The National Parliament took the first vote on Constitutional Amendment No. 43 (Dual Citizenship), which also lets the Minister naturalise investors under a new s. 67(4)(b): 90 of 111 seats voted for, none against.
events.quote: the first vote was taken on 3 November 2015 when the number of seats in the National Parliament were 111 and those voting for the proposal were 90 and none voted against the proposal

events.title: Second parliamentary vote on the dual citizenship constitutional amendment
events.description: Second vote on Constitutional Amendment No. 43: 91 of 111 seats voted for, none against; the law was certified on 29 Aug 2016.
events.quote: the second vote was taken on 31 March 2016 when the number of seats in the National Parliament were 111 and those voting for the proposal were 91 and none voted against the proposal.

events.title: EUR 65,000 holding must be invested in fixed assets; large-investor direct investment defined
events.description: From 1 July 2020 (RT I, 17.06.2020, 2) the EUR 65,000 for an enterprise permit must be invested in share capital used to acquire real estate, machinery or equipment registered as fixed assets in Estonia, the separate validity rule for enterprise permits was repealed, and the large investor's direct investment was defined (share capital for fixed assets, investments in active Estonian companies or in an investment fund).
events.quote: An alien who has a holding in a company shall have invested at least 65,000 euros in the share capital of an Estonian company, for which real estate, machinery or equipment has been acquired and registered as fixed assets in Estonia.

events.title: EUR 65,000 requirement waived for young companies backed by state or licensed private investors
events.description: From 1 January 2026 (RT I, 17.04.2025, 2) the EUR 65,000 holding is not required if the company has been registered for less than 12 months and starts operating with investment or a loan from the state or a fund manager licensed by the Financial Supervision Authority, or with public support.
events.quote: the company has been entered in the Estonian commercial register for less than 12 months and commences operation with the support of the state or private investments

events.title: Ordonnance 3.153 sets Monaco residence cards
events.description: Sovereign Ordinance 3.153 of 19 March 1964 (Journal de Monaco 20 March 1964) on entry and stay of foreigners: residence cards for over-16s, first card on a work permit or proof of sufficient means of existence plus housing; temporary, ordinary and privileged cards (validities as later amended in 1996).
events.quote: soit les pièces justificatives de moyens suffisants d'existence, s'il n'entend exercer aucune profession.

ledger.contains: IMPO consolidated text of Decreto 148/007 (personal income tax, IRPF, regulations) as updated to Decreto 225/026 of 16 Sep 2026. In scope: art. 5-BIS (tax residence: days of presence, 30-day sporadic absences, base of activities, family presumption, investment criteria a)-d): real estate over 15m UI; company over 45m UI in projects of national interest; real estate over 3.5m UI from 1 Jul 2020 with 60 days presence; company over 15m UI from 1 Jul 2020 with 15 new jobs) with amendment notes; art. 5-QUATER and 5-QUINQUIES (IRNR options for new residents, 10 years, real estate over 3.5m UI from 22 Jan 2021, options closing 31 Dec 2025); 5-SEXIES and 5-SEPTIES (impatriate capital-income regime conditions: real estate over 12.5m UI or 625,000 UI a year in funds; 50% rate for 5 years with 6.25m UI; fixed tax 1.25m UI a year with company investment over 45m UI). The four residence thresholds were already in program_terms; presence, jobs, tax-benefit thresholds and dated decrees added. The rest of the decree (general IRPF rules, deductions, rates, withholding) is out of scope.

IMPO page of Decreto 163/020 (promulgated 11 Jun 2020, published 12 Jun 2020): recitals on investment promotion and the need to adjust the tax-residence regime to promote foreign investment; article 1 gave new wording to art. 5-BIS inciso 5 literals c) and d) of Decreto 148/007 (the amended text itself is shown only in the consolidated decree, where literal c) was later reworded by Decreto 174/020). No numbers on the page. Covered by event e-0fc92a0d6c; the amounts are recorded from ury-impo-dec148-2007.

IMPO consolidated text of the Migration Law 18.250 (6 Jan 2008, as amended): rights of migrants, admission categories (non-resident, temporary resident incl. business people, entrepreneurs, directors, managers and consultants; permanent resident for relatives of Uruguayans and Mercosur nationals, decision within 90 working days), entry, stay, expulsion, institutions, offences. No investor category and no investment amounts; already used for event e-b62f48983b. Nothing further in scope.

Bill 8586 as deposited (21 Jul 2025, 48 pp.): transposition of the Single Permit Directive (EU) 2024/1233, repeal of the investor residence title (arts. 53bis-53quater, art. 5 of the bill) and changes to family reunification of beneficiaries of international protection; exposé des motifs with the investor table (9 titles since 2017: 2018 4, 2019 2, 2020 1, 2024 2; first 7 not renewed), commentary (introduced by the law of 20 March 2017, prior opinion by Economy/Finance ministries, controls hard to carry out, self-employed permit remains), consolidated text, correspondence table, financial note (no foreseeable expenditure), sustainability check and impact sheet (image pages 35-47, read by OCR; no programme numbers). Table parts add up to the printed total of 9. Family reunification figures (e.g. 469 permits in 2024) are out of scope. Counts and the abolition event were already recorded; permit validity and the 2017 launch date added.

Ministry of Finance FAQ (created May 2018) on the investor residence title under art. 53bis of the law of 8 March 2017 (as the FAQ names it): purpose (real-estate investments excluded), the four investment options (EUR 500,000 existing company kept 5 years; EUR 500,000 new company kept 3 years; EUR 3 million investment structure; EUR 20 million deposit kept 5 years), competent ministries, 3-year validity and annual follow-up, procedure (90-day provisional permit, derogatory procedure, arrival within 3 days, application within 3 months), criteria for the structure (2 full-time employees, 75% own funds, substance) and the deposit (100% own funds, single bank, monthly-average check), documents, forms of opinion, annual verification, renewal. The four amounts were already recorded; validity and the other numbered conditions added. No statistics. Note: the FAQ dates the law 8 March 2017, Bill 8586 says 20 March 2017.

Draft Government decision (Feb 2020, PM Ion Chicu) approving a bill for a moratorium until 1 Jan 2021 on new applications under art. 17(11)-(12) of Citizenship Law 1024/2000 (citizenship by investment); pending applications to be examined as set by the Government; 2019 contracts of accredited agents extended by the moratorium period without the fee of annex 3 pt. 4 of HG 786/2017; informative note (Ministry of Economy and Infrastructure: a repeated moratorium to allow a final decision on the programme; no extra budget cost). No numbers. Covered by event e-5e85d6b6b2.

Consultation draft (Word, 20 Mar 2018) amending Government Decision 786/2017 on citizenship by investment: due diligence by a company contracted by the Commission; reputation checks extended to dependent family members aged 16 or more (draft pt. 7^1); applications via an information system or the Commission secretariat; Commission to select by tender an exclusive company to design, implement and promote the programme for up to 5 years, extendable by up to 3, paid by applicants through a commission, no public money; bidder criteria (at least 5 years of CBI experience, forecasts of programme investment, free application and due-diligence IT systems); programme start within 3 months of the contract. Draft provisions, not confirmed as adopted, so not recorded as programme terms; covered by event e-5eca14bc42. No statistics.

PacLII text (Wayback capture) of the Citizenship (Amendment) Act 2016, No. 42 of 2016, certified 22 Dec 2016: renunciation and dual citizenship for persons under 19, new s. 6A (sportsperson naturalisation), s. 6B (investor naturalisation: business and investment background, record of creating employment and imparting skills, whether the applicant held the relevant investor visa, language, other connection; prescribed form and fee; part of the fee refunded on refusal), s. 6C (dual citizenship), Citizenship Advisory Committee ad hoc members (30 days), s. 12 fees set by instrument of the finance minister with power to waive or reduce, new forms 1, 1A and 7. No amounts or statistics (fees left to an instrument). Covered by event e-1b6c32d095.

PacLII text (Wayback capture) of Constitutional Amendment No. 43 (Dual Citizenship) Law 2016, certified 29 Aug 2016: privacy and biometrics (s. 49), dual citizenship (s. 64), citizenship by descent and marriage with 12 months residence in the preceding three years (s. 66), naturalisation of sportspersons and of investors with the resources, capital, commitment and credentials to invest and create employment, exempt from the requirement in s. 67(2)(c) (s. 67(4)-(6)), withdrawal of such citizenship for false representation (s. 70(4)), binding unanimous committee refusals (s. 76(6)); Speaker's certificate of the two votes (3 Nov 2015: 90 for, 0 against of 111 seats; 31 Mar 2016: 91 for, 0 against). Vote counts are parliamentary figures, recorded only in the two vote events, not as observations. No programme amounts.

Barbados Immigration Department page listing requirements for a Special Entry Permit (application under s. 13(3) of the Immigration Act, Form B): photographs, civil documents, passport, police certificates from countries of residence of six months or more in the last three years, title deeds and land tax bills, proof of financial resources, health insurance valid in Barbados, proof of dependants, translations, application fee BDS $300 payable on submission. No investment or net-worth threshold. The fee was already recorded; nothing else in scope with a programme amount.

TSE compilation (171 pp.) of the 2012 Reglamento de Extranjería: definitions (investor: own capital in activities of economic and social interest), general fees and guarantee deposit, requirements for each temporary and permanent residence and special category (pensioners, rentistas, investors, workers, students, etc.), documentation and renewal. In scope: investor articles 87-93 (US$200,000 minimum in real estate, registrable goods, shares, securities, productive or national-interest projects; US$50 application fee; documents by investment type; forestry route with US$100,000 initial investment and a 3-year management plan; no paid work), art. 179 (fees on approval: Law art. 251 amount, US$30 + US$30, US$25 a year, guarantee deposit) and art. 223 (renewal every two years with proof of the investment). The US$200,000 threshold was already recorded; fees, forestry route and renewal added. Other categories (pensionado, rentista, etc.) are not investment routes and are out of scope. No statistics.

Presidency news item (19 Mar 2024): ProDominicana adds the Migration Directorate's investor-residence procedures to the single investment window (VUI) under the Burocracia Cero programme; the VUI then had 33 integrated procedures, 19 institutions and 6 municipalities (counts about the window, not the residence programme, so not recorded). No thresholds or programme counts. Covered by event e-819e3b8dde.

Official English translation of the Estonian Aliens Act (consolidated, in force 1 Jan-21 May 2026; ~500 KB of text): visas incl. start-up visas, temporary stay, immigration quota (0.1% of population, exemptions incl. large investors), temporary residence permits (validity up to 5 years, extension up to 10 years) for family, study, employment, enterprise (§§ 191-197: EUR 65,000 in fixed assets or EUR 16,000 for sole proprietors, start-up and new-company exemptions, alternatives after one year of EUR 200,000 turnover or social tax on 5x average wage, refusal and revocation grounds) and large investors (§§ 197^2-197^8: EUR 1 million direct investment or fund, lasting investment, no dwelling requirement), permanent residence, EU long-term residence, removal, data processing, supervision. Investment thresholds already in the data; alternatives, validity, quota and two dated amendments added. Other permit types (employment, study, family, start-up employment, digital nomad) are out of scope. No statistics.

Undated ANEF checklist (4 pp.) of supporting documents for the passeport talent residence card as investor or holder of an economic project: personal documents and proof of address; investor (French Tech Visa for investors: EUR 300,000 direct investment in fixed assets personally or via a company run or at least 30% owned, jobs created or saved within four years; documents for first issue, renewal, change of status); business creator (master or 5 years experience, EUR 30,000 invested, resources at least the full-time minimum wage, Bpifrance certificate); innovative project founder (French Tech Visa for founders); corporate officer (3 months in the group, gross pay of at least EUR 54,763.80, i.e. 3 times the annual minimum wage). Only the investor category belongs to this programme; the business-creator, founder and corporate-officer categories are other passeport talent grounds and are not recorded. Investor amount already recorded; ownership share and job deadline added. No statistics.

Scanned Ghana Investment Promotion Authority Bill 2026 (45 pp., all pages read by OCR): memorandum; establishment, governance and finances of the Authority; entry and admission of foreign investors (sector-based minimum foreign capital, reserved activities); registration; tax incentives; clause 39 directing the Ministry of the Interior to enact citizenship-by-investment legislation (no amounts or timetable); investment guarantees, grievances; expatriate quotas for registered enterprises by invested capital (clause 46: US$50,000-500,000 two persons up to more than US$10 million twelve persons, valid 5 years) and work permits; technology transfer; offences. Only clause 39 concerns a citizenship/residence-by-investment programme and is covered by event e-967dad6d5a; the expatriate quotas are work-permit entitlements of companies, not an investor residence route, and foreign capital minimums are business-entry rules, so neither is recorded. There is no Ghana programme row.

Unofficial consolidated Croatian Aliens Act (Zakon o strancima, NN 133/20 to 55/26 per zakon.hr): entry, visas, short stay, temporary residence (family, study, research, etc.), residence and work permits (quotas abolished; employers; seasonal work; art. 110 categories incl. self-employment with 51% ownership and strategic investment projects; art. 113 key staff and self-employed sole owners: EUR 26,544.56 capital or investment, three Croatian employees, salary 1.5 times average; art. 115 strategic investment projects decided within 15 days; validity up to 2 years under art. 110), Blue Card, intra-corporate transfers, long-term residence, return, detention, fines (employer, carrier fines out of scope). Not a passive investor visa. The EUR 26,544.56 threshold was already recorded; employment, salary, ownership and validity conditions added. Employer fines and other permit types are out of scope. No statistics.

Consolidated Lithuanian Law on the Legal Status of Aliens (IX-2206, version 1 Jul-31 Oct 2026, 143 pp.): entry, visas, temporary residence grounds (work, Blue Card with EUR 1 million company revenue condition for managers, family reunification incl. exemption for investors in state-important projects, studies, lawful activity art. 45: company participant with EUR 28,000 equity incl. EUR 14,000 own investment and wage bill of 2 average wages; EUR 260,000 investment with 5 jobs; manager of a EUR 500,000 company with 10 jobs; 1/3 shareholding; permit for 2 years; refusal/revocation if the company is fictitious or no longer meets art. 45(1)(1), (1^1), (2^2)), permanent residence, EU long-term residence, expulsion, asylum, amendment notes. Investor thresholds (14,000; 260,000) and the 2016 event were already recorded; the other art. 45 conditions and validity added. Work, Blue Card, study, family and asylum provisions are out of scope. No statistics.

Consolidated Sovereign Ordinance 3.153 of 19 March 1964 on entry and stay of foreigners in Monaco (Legimonaco): passport and French entry conditions, residence card application within 8 days (over 16), housing proof, card types (temporary up to 1 year; ordinary after 3 years, valid 3 years; Monegasque spouse card 5 years; privileged after 10 years, valid 10 years), conditions (work permit or sufficient means), lodging registration by hotels and landlords, sanctions (fines in old francs) and expulsion. No minimum amount of money; validity and qualifying periods added as terms; the 1964 ordinance recorded as the launch event (programs.csv already gives 1964-03-19). No statistics.

DOF text of the 2012 Lineamientos para trámites y procedimientos migratorios (Secretaría de Gobernación): definitions and general rules, then procedure sheets (fichas) for visas, entry, status changes, regularisation, permanent residence, documents, with fees by reference to the Ley Federal de Derechos (no amounts printed), maximum decision times and validity. In scope: the investor case for temporary residence (shareholding or business fixed assets worth 20,000 days of minimum wage, or business with at least five formal jobs; repeated in arts. 41, 43, 52), the real-estate case (40,000 days), validity (1-3 years on change of status, up to 4 years) and decision times (20 working days). The investor amount was already recorded; real estate, jobs, validity and processing time added. Economic-solvency cases (bank balances of 20,000 days or income of 400 days a month), employment offers, students and invitations are not investment routes and are not recorded. No statistics.

Samoa Citizenship Investment Regulations 2016 (scanned, 5 pp., read by OCR): citation and commencement with the Act, interpretation, submission of application and fees to the Committee secretary, appointment and criteria of due diligence persons and a list of them, due diligence checks and report, payment of due diligence fees (up to 50% upfront), Minister may set a minimum number of employees for an investor's business (no number), Schedule of fees (application WST 120,000 principal, spouse 120,000, children 60,000/60,000/120,000; due diligence 20,000 principal, spouse 20,000, children 0/5,000/10,000; promotion application 1,000; agency application 50,000). Application and due diligence fees were already recorded (family amounts in applies_to); agency and promotion fees and the payment split added. Signature date partly illegible (12th day, month and year not legible). No statistics.
